questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location and size of university and student community. Also, the possible experience at the location such as skiing and exploring nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great welcome and organization at the host university. Full of learning opportunities.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Great introduction emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Communication with the local exchange contact person.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very challenging finding accommodation. I would recommend to apply as early as possible to local dorms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are a few dorms located central in Innsbruck, Apply to these as soon as possible. It is easier to receive a shared room compared to a single room. Living centrally in Innsbruck also means you are close to the hospital and medical university. If you live further out, transportation by bus is super easy and you can catch any bus almost every 10min throughout the day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online form was to be filled out in order to pick up your student card at the university. Another physical registration process by the local exchange coordinator was also required and very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Local exchange coordinator was available for questions. Welcome and information meeting,

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not take any classes, however registration for clinical rotation at the hospital was unproblematic.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact the exchange coordinator at the host university as soon as possible to wish for which department you want, for the clinical rotation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did not take any courses, just clinical rotation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Teaching in hospital was similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 3 month clinical rotation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not take any courses, but the surgical department VTT at the hospital was great for clinical rotation aswell as intensive care (ACI) and orthopedics.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The ESN (Erasmus student network) is hosting a lot of activities every week such as pub-crawls, friend dating, creative activities, field trips etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go skiing! The mountains are great.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Meet friends in the city for a coffee/matcha, going skiing or visiting the nearby countries and cities. Italy is very close, as well as Germany.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the ESN activities!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Here you refer to strangers in a polite form of you in German.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The mountain live and work life balance!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: bring cash, enjoy the mountains and start looking for accommodation in time

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Practice your German. The Austrian German is different and can be hard to understand when you ar enot used to hearing it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience in the mountains and the friends I made through uni.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language, Austrian German is challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Innsbruck!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
